rows.current: Allows to filter/remove specific ROI metadata entries
rows.name: Remove/Filter 2D ROI metadata

rows.current: Creates a color image in which the 2D ROIs from the input image's overlay are drawn over the image. It takes an ImageJ image and produces a color ImageJ image, applying the selected outline, fill, label, opacity, and magnification settings.
rows.name: Render overlay

rows.current: Rotates all ROI in the ROI list. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Rotate 2D ROI (old)

rows.current: Scales all ROI in the ROI list. If you want to have more flexibility, use one of the 'Change ROI properties' nodes. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available.
rows.name: Scale 2D ROI (old)

rows.current: Associates an image to the ROI. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Set 2D ROI image

rows.current: Sets ROI metadata by statistics. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Set 2D ROI metadata by statistics (expression)

rows.current: Sets the ROI metadata (property map) from a table. The table either has a column that indicates the ROI index or contains one row per ROI (row index is the ROI index) This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Set 2D ROI metadata from table

rows.current: Sets properties of all Roi to values extracted from annotations.
rows.name: Set 2D ROI properties from annotations

rows.current: Sets properties of all ROI to values extracted from a table. Table rows are matched to their ROI and the column values are put into expression variables, so the ROI can be modified. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Set 2D ROI properties from table

rows.current: Sorts a ROI list according to an expression-defined property. Has access to annotations and measurements. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Sort 2D ROI list (expression)

rows.current: Algorithm that extracts connected components across one or multiple dimensions. The output consists of multiple ROI lists, one for each connected component. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Split 2D ROI into connected components

rows.current: Converts the ROI into point ROI that are the centroids of their inputs
rows.name: Outline 2D ROI (Centroid)

rows.current: Applies rotation, scaling, and translation of 2D ROI. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.

rows.current: Removes any association of the ROI from any image.
rows.name: Clear 2D ROI image

rows.current: Performs segmentation via watershed on a 2D or 3D image using flooding simulations. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Classic watershed

rows.current: Applies a 3x3 sharpening filter. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. This node supports various methods: Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold) If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Mean/Median/MidGrey/Otsu, 8-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. This node supports various methods: Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold) If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Mean/Median/MidGrey/Otsu, 16-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Bernsen recommends a radius of 15 and a contrast threshold of 15.
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Bernsen, 16-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Based on a simple contrast toggle. This procedure does not have user-provided parameters other than the kernel radius. Sets the pixel value to either white or black depending on whether its current value is closest to the local Max or Min respectively. The procedure is similar to Toggle Contrast Enhancement (see Soille, Morphological Image Analysis (2004), p. 259
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Contrast, 16-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Niblack, 16-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. The threshold is calculated as t = mean * (1 + p * exp(-q * mean) + k * ((stdev / r) - 1)). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Phansalkar, 16-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Sauvola, 16-bit)

rows.current: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.

rows.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Sauvola, 8-bit)

rows.name: Manual threshold 2D (16-bit)

rows.current: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Manual threshold 2D (32-bit)

rows.current: Thresholds LAB images.
rows.name: Manual color threshold (LAB)

rows.current: Thresholds the image with a threshold calculated from the image pixel values (percentile of the 65536-bin histogram). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Percentile threshold 2D (16-bit)

rows.current: Thresholds the image with a threshold calculated from the image pixel values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Percentile threshold 2D (8-bit)

rows.current: Crops the incoming images to fit into the boundaries defined by the ROI. Alternative: Extract to ROI This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Crop image to 2D ROI

rows.current: Makes all images within a iteration step have the same size by padding with the predefined background color according to the largest image dimensions. If you want more control (source/target) and/or also want to do the same for Z/C/T, use 'Equalize hyperstack dimensions' This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
rows.name: Make images equal 2D (single input)

rows.current: Pads each image slice with a background color. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Expand canvas 2D

rows.current: The two endpoints of a line a provided via expressions. The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Mirror image over line 2D (Expressions)

rows.current: The two endpoints of a line a provided via one or multiple line ROI. If multiple ROI are provided, the algorithm is executed per ROI. If a ROI is not a line ROI, a line outline/hull operation is applied to the ROI (see Outline 2D ROI).The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Mirror image over line 2D (ROI)

rows.current: Rotates the image by any kind of angle. Expands the canvas if necessary. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Rotate 2D image (free)

rows.current: Aligns slices in the input image to other slices using methods implemented by TurboReg and MultiStackReg. Due to the variation in registration tasks, this node follows a 'rules' approach where each slice of the input image is matched to one rule that determines how the slice is aligned. There are three modes: (1) register to a reference slice, (2) use the same transformation calculated for another slice, and (3) apply no registration. Use the examples provided via the 'Tools' menu (top right of the parameter window) to get started with configuring the rules. Handling of RGB images: as the underlying alignment methods were only designed for greyscale images, RGB slices are automatically converted to greyscale prior to registration (using ImageJ methods). The resulting transformation is then applied per RGB channel, which is then output. Please note that if an RGB image is present, the output will be RGB. You may lose greyscale precision (16 bit/ 32 bit) in other slices. To prevent this, convert RGB to greyscale prior to registration (e.g. by splitting RGB channels into hyperstack channels). This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: TurboReg registration 2D (simple)

rows.current: Subtracts a blurred copy of the image and rescales the image to obtain the same contrast of large (low-frequency) structures as in the input image. This is equivalent to adding a high-pass filtered image and thus sharpens the image. "Radius (Sigma)" is the standard deviation (blur radius) of the Gaussian blur that is subtracted. "Mask Weight" determines the strength of filtering, where "Mask Weight"=1 would be an infinite weight of the high-pass filtered image that is added. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Unsharp mask 2D

rows.current: Exports incoming images into a non-JIPipe format (PNG, JPEG, BMP, AVI, TIFF). Please note support for input images depending on the file format: PNG, JPEG, BMP: 2D images only AVI: 2D or 3D images only TIFF: All images supported This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Export image (directory slot)

rows.current: Annotates data with metadata extracted from OME metadata This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
rows.name: Annotate data with OME image metadata

rows.current: Applies thresholding by applying a background subtraction, auto thresholding, and various morphological operations. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. If you want to further customize all steps, create a group or set of nodes that apply the following operations: Subtract background (rolling ball): default radius = 20 Auto threshold 2D Morphological dilation Morphological hole filling Morphological erosion Optional: Gaussian blur
rows.name: Bright spots segmentation 2D

rows.current: Finds circular 2D objects via a Hough transform. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
rows.name: Detect circles 2D (Hough)
